newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil eases with crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil eases with crude.

text.p: High sulphur cracked fuel oil prices in Europe slipped again on Thursday amid relatively slack demand and weaker crude oil futures, traders said.

High sulphur barges traded early at $111 fob ARA but offers then fell heavily to as low as $107, with little buying interest seen. "It is a combination of weaker crude and very little bunker demand," one ARA trader said.

High sulphur cargoes were steady to softer, after the sale of an ex-ARA cargo to a utility on Wednesday at $110 cif NWE. In the Med, a major on Wednesday sold an early Jan Isab cargo at at 50 cents over the average of February's high fob quotes.

Another trader's Isab cargo, which had been heard offered in the Med on Wednesday as low as $104 fob Med, was eventually placed into one of the trader's commitments into a recent Maltese tender. Med swaps were softer again, talked at around $101 fob, around $8 below the mean of current fob quotes.
Low sulphur prices were easier, under relentless good supply. An oil major offered a cargo at $110.50 fob NWE, but buying interest was again slack.
Swaps were softer, however, and February was talked at around $108/$109 fob NWE.
